teaser: Week 27: you take the 4-week canary live at 5% of clinicians, arm the rollback gates, and hand Meridian's system to the on-call team.

scene.title: The canary goes live: rollback gates, runbooks and the handoff
scene.sceneHtml:
Evaluation suite passing, Week 27. The deployment plan is approved: a 4-week canary rollout starting with 5% of clinical documentation users, expanding to 25%, 50%, then 100% if quality gates pass at each stage. The Head of Engineering asks: "What triggers an automatic rollback? How do we communicate progress to the clinical staff and the board?" The compliance team adds: "We need runbooks for the three most likely incident scenarios."

Your final deliverables: a canary deployment plan with rollback gates, stakeholder communication templates, operational runbooks, and a handoff package for the operations team.

takeaways: Canary rollout 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%; automated rollback gates revert the release if any metric breaches its threshold at any stage.
Define SLOs and the metrics/slices to monitor before building dashboards and alerts; write runbooks for the top 3 incident scenarios.
Technical handoff package = architecture overview, ADRs, component diagrams, runbooks and known limitations, not meeting notes.
Fixed, predictable steps → workflow (lower latency, predictable cost); open-ended → agent. Sub-50ms scoring or exact math → not Claude.
